# Hexalith.Platform

Platform-owned Aspire host for Hexalith domain modules.

This repository is the **EXT-HOST-1** delivery target for Hexalith Agents: it owns
production-like composition of the Agents DomainService and FrontComposer UI with
EventStore, Conversations, Parties, Tenants, Provider and safety adapters, Dapr
Workflow, secrets, health, identity, telemetry, and evidence ingress.

Domain modules such as [Hexalith.Agents](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.Agents)
must **not** ship module-owned `AppHost`, `Aspire`, or `ServiceDefaults` projects.
Those hosting concerns live here.

## Status

| Milestone | State |
| --- | --- |
| Repository + empty Aspire AppHost scaffold | Current |
| Works development topology | Opt-in preview; AD-20 parity gate open |
| Agents DomainService / UI composition wiring | Planned (Agents Story 5.6) |
| Live Level 4/5 compatibility evidence | Planned (`Available` gate) |

## Requirements

- .NET SDK `10.0.402` or later (`latestPatch` roll-forward)
- Aspire CLI `13.6.1` exactly. The module tool compares `aspire --version` with
  the catalog-selected `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` and refuses any other version with
  `HXR015`.

## Module tool

From the Platform root, restore and check its exact local tool pin:

```bash
dotnet tool restore
dotnet tool run hexalith-module --version
```

The local tool manifest pins `hexalith.builds.module.cli` `4.35.2`, accepted for
Platform `run`, `debug` and opt-in domain enrollment validation.
`hexalith-platform.json` accepts versions in `[4.35.2, 5.0.0-0)`.
The floor includes corrected Story 1.13 adoption checks for real workspaces.
Later 4.x releases, prereleases included, are accepted without a Platform edit; 5.0
prereleases are excluded. The catalog commit is
`4248b8c70cb35ba79fdd7e4dd63049d4c73211a0`, matching release tag `v4.35.2`.
The pinned tool's run/debug topology, SDK and Dapr/Aspire pins are unchanged from
`4.34.0`; its package catalog selects EventStore `3.126.1`, Tenants `5.10.0` and
Parties `1.5.1`. Only the pinned version is guaranteed to embed that catalog.
Another accepted 4.x tool brings its own embedded Dapr, Redis and AppHost SDK
pins, and nothing compares them with the catalog yet. When the exact pin moves,
the Builds gitlink moves to that version's release-tag commit.
See the [Story 1.13 evidence](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/evidence/1-13/README.md)
for owner approval, gated publication and fresh released-tool acceptance. The
[Story 1.11 evidence](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/evidence/1-11/README.md)
records McpCli, EventStore and Memories verification with `4.34.0`; the
[Story 1.10 evidence](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/evidence/1-10/README.md)
records the earlier EventStore and Memories proof with `4.33.1`.

Versions below the configured range are not Platform-accepted, including
`4.34.0`, `4.35.0` and `4.35.1`. Version `4.34.0` first built McpCli; `4.33.1` composed only
servers. The earlier `4.33.0` also had a mismatched packaged Tooling identity and build-machine paths.
From `4.31.0`, a tool outside the range is refused with `HXW010` in package mode
and warned in source mode. Older tools do not check the range, so run the pinned
tool through `dotnet tool run`.

The canonical [candidate evidence and attachment policy v1](docs/contracts/candidate-and-attachment-policy-v1.md)
fixes committed PR merge-result evidence, prohibits reuse across decisions and
sets finite attachment holds. This publishes Platform policy for downstream
descriptor and runner adoption; it does not establish implemented support or
change the accepted tool pin. Accepting attachments under it requires Builds
adoption; accepting evidence also requires a Platform-accepted, integration-qualified tool.

The versioned [test environment and terminal result contracts](docs/contracts/test-environment-v1.md)
publish strict, offline-readable schemas for runner endpoints, composition identity,
reserved candidate proof, attachment holds and the four terminal outcomes. Builds
ships the schemas and consumer reader; lifecycle and evidence adoption remain
downstream responsibilities.

## Parties reference domain

The qualified independent `Hexalith.Parties` checkout pins module tool `4.34.0`
against its own direct Platform gitlink `17179e5`, whose accepted range is
`[4.34.0, 5.0.0-0)`. That historical qualification does not change this checkout's
current minimum above. From that Parties checkout:

```bash
dotnet tool restore
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
```

Parties declares EventStore, Tenants and Memories, giving seven ready servers
including `parties`; source and Debug bindings use only the tool-selected direct
references. Platform routes the singular `party` domain to `parties/process`,
binds the existing state/pubsub keys and renders the declarative tenant subscription.
Rich Parties search stays disabled. Legacy domain AppHost, Aspire, UI/MCP and sample
hosts remain frozen outside this qualification. Owner review and upstream
integration are complete; the [Story 1.12 evidence](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/evidence/1-12/README.md)
records that qualification and its exact revisions. Story 1.12 predates the
enrollment kit: Parties is not enrolled under `validate --adoption`. Its current
checkout still has programmatic subscription discovery, literal Dapr component
names, a missing hosting inventory and the older pin. Those changes belong to
Parties' owner-led enrollment; see the
[Story 1.13 findings](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-13-publish-the-domain-module-enrollment-kit.md#review-findings).

## Run and debug a technical module

EventStore, Memories and McpCli run and debug from this workspace, never from
their own repository. Each command takes the owner manifest in the module's
checkout under `references/`; the tool loads every owner manifest itself, so
never pass the copies in `src/Hexalith.Platform.Composition/Declarations/` (that
duplicates a module and fails with `HXP003`/`HXP020`).

| Module | Manifest | Platform runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EventStore | `references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json` | `eventstore` |
| Memories | `references/Hexalith.Memories/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json` | `memories`, `memories-access-telemetry-clock`, `memories-access-telemetry`, `eventstore`, plus Redis Stack (`memories-vectors`) and FalkorDB (`memories-graph`); no Tenants |
| McpCli | `references/Hexalith.McpCli/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json` | `eventstore` (the gateway McpCli targets), plus a run-scoped Debug build of `references/Hexalith.McpCli`; McpCli declares no server or interface |

### Prerequisites

- The pinned tool (`dotnet tool restore`), the .NET SDK and Aspire CLI
  `13.6.1` listed above, and a running Docker engine.
- The direct submodules `references/Hexalith.Builds`, `references/Hexalith.EventStore`,
  `references/Hexalith.Tenants` and `references/Hexalith.Memories`, initialized
  without `--recursive`. The tool reads all three declaration owners even for
  EventStore alone; the selected resources remain those in the table above.
  McpCli also needs `references/Hexalith.McpCli`, with its own nested
  `references/*` left uninitialized (`HXW003` refuses any initialized nested
  submodule).
  Each checkout's `HEAD` must equal the gitlink staged in this
  repository. After a local commit inside a submodule, stage it with
  `git add references/<Repository>` or the tool refuses the run.
- The local Aspire orchestration and dashboard packages at `13.6.1`. From this
  workspace, run `dotnet restore apphost.cs` once before the first `run` or `debug`.
  Tool restore alone does not install these SDK packages. If NuGet uses a custom
  `globalPackagesFolder`, set `NUGET_PACKAGES` to that absolute folder for both
  restore and `debug`; the tool otherwise checks `~/.nuget/packages` and reports
  `HXR016` when the required packages are missing.
- `HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME`: an absolute, isolated Dapr home with Dapr CLI `1.18.0`
  at `tools/dapr` and runtime `1.18.2` at `.dapr/bin/{daprd,placement,scheduler}`.
  A machine-wide `dapr init` does not qualify. On Linux x64 (including WSL2),
  prepare one from the official release assets; other platforms need the
  matching `<os>_<arch>` assets of the same releases. The subshell stops at the
  first failed download or checksum, removes its downloads and leaves your shell
  where it was:

  ```bash
  (
    set -euo pipefail
    dapr_home="$HOME/.hexalith/dapr/1.18.2"
    mkdir -p "$dapr_home/tools" "$dapr_home/.dapr/bin"
    downloads="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$downloads"' EXIT
    cd "$downloads"
    base=https://github.com/dapr
    for asset in cli/releases/download/v1.18.0/dapr_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
        dapr/releases/download/v1.18.2/daprd_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
        dapr/releases/download/v1.18.2/placement_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
        dapr/releases/download/v1.18.2/scheduler_linux_amd64.tar.gz; do
      curl -fsSLO "$base/$asset"
      curl -fsSLO "$base/$asset.sha256"
    done
    sha256sum -c ./*.sha256
    tar -xzf dapr_linux_amd64.tar.gz -C "$dapr_home/tools"
    for binary in daprd placement scheduler; do
      tar -xzf "${binary}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -C "$dapr_home/.dapr/bin"
    done
    DAPR_RUNTIME_PATH="$dapr_home" "$dapr_home/tools/dapr" --version   # CLI 1.18.0, runtime 1.18.2
  )
  ```

### Commands

From the Platform root:

```bash
export HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME="$HOME/.hexalith/dapr/1.18.2"

# EventStore alone
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.EventStore/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json

# Memories with its EventStore dependency
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest references/Hexalith.Memories/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.Memories/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json

# McpCli with the EventStore gateway it targets
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- debug --manifest references/Hexalith.McpCli/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- down --manifest references/Hexalith.McpCli/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
```

`debug` builds the active module and its root-declared dependencies from their
`references/` checkouts in Debug, waits for each server's declared `/ready`
endpoint (10-minute default deadline), and reports one process id per project.
`run` starts the same composition without reporting process ids. `down` stops
only the resources tagged with that run. Each signed runner plan and direct file
AppHost allocates its own Sentry, placement, scheduler and sidecar listeners;
persisted runner ports are honored. Each run owns its Redis, scheduler data,
Memories vector/graph data, issuer credentials, secrets and SQLite discovery registry
outside the checkout. Allocation probes release their sockets before startup;
a competing bind fails startup instead of selecting shared resources.

Set `HEXALITH_DAPR_HOME` to an installation containing the catalog-pinned CLI at
`tools/dapr` and native runtime at `.dapr/bin/daprd` (plus placement/scheduler for
Builds prerequisite checks). Installed binaries and component templates can be
shared read-only. Ordinary file-entry and runner `debug`/`run` project launches
use the checkout's shared developer build outputs (`bin`, `obj` and configured
`artifacts` paths); concurrent builds can contend there. Runner test suites select
private project outputs under their run workspace. Build outputs are developer
inputs to composition; the runtime data and credentials listed above are run-owned.
The file entry also accepts the user's installed native runtime
when no home is selected. An unavailable selected runtime fails startup.
`Dapr:Mtls:CertificateDirectory` selects an external parent for a private child per
run; checkout paths, including symlinks into the checkout, are rejected.

Reference compositions start their own Redis, never consume dapr-init Redis or
acquire exported fixture locks, and instantiate no Keycloak. Legacy technical
own-repository fixtures are outside Platform integration evidence; descriptor
migration is Story 2.9. Works remains an opt-in development preview with its existing
qualification scope. See [concurrency verification](docs/platform-apphost-form.md)
for the gated two-session proof and its current evidence limits.

McpCli is a short-lived CLI, not a server. For the McpCli manifest, `run` and
`debug` also build `references/Hexalith.McpCli/src/Hexalith.McpCli`
in Debug into the run workspace, using the run's pinned Builds catalog. `test`
needs `--profile` naming a declared test; the McpCli declaration declares none,
so `test` refuses it (`HXC002`) and builds nothing. The
build never packs or publishes the tool and never writes the checkout's `bin`
or `obj`. When the environment is ready, an `HXI010` diagnostic with field
`mcpcli` names the built tool,
`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/hexalith-builds/g4-workspaces/<runId>/tools/mcpcli/bin/Hexalith.McpCli/debug/Hexalith.McpCli.dll`,
and the checkout project it was built from; `down` deletes it with the run
workspace. A missing checkout or tool project fails with `HXW004`, and a failed
build with `HXR020`, before any resource starts. Both name McpCli and the
expected project path; no other copy, such as a sibling `../mcpcli` checkout,
is used. Package mode builds no McpCli; package-mode McpCli arrives in Epic 3.
The started EventStore gateway is the target of connected execution, which also
arrives in Epic 3; the debugger recipe below uses offline verbs only. The build
first shipped in `4.34.0`; use the current accepted range above. The earlier `4.33.1`
composes only servers and builds no McpCli; it is outside the range, so it is
warned (`HXW010`) in source mode and refused in package mode.

`debug` does not print the run id. It is the file name of the run state
`<runId>.json` under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/hexalith-builds/g4-runs/`
on Linux. Inspect the state files and select the one whose `projectProcessIds`
contains the launcher id reported by this `debug` invocation. Confirm its
`manifestHash` matches `sha256sum <manifest>` (ignoring hexadecimal letter case),
then use its `runId`. File modification time alone cannot identify your run.
When an earlier run used the same manifest, `down --manifest` refuses with
`HXR024`; pass the id as `down --manifest <manifest> --run-id <runId>`.
An explicit `--run-id` chooses that run directly; the tool does not cross-check
its manifest, so verify both fields before stopping it.

### Attach a debugger

The reported process id is the `dotnet run` launcher, not the application. The
application is the launcher's child process:

```bash
ps --ppid <launcher-pid> -o pid,args
```

Attach to the child whose command is the module's
`bin/Debug/net10.0/<Assembly>` executable, for example with VS Code
("Attach to a .NET process"). Breakpoints bind to the sources in
`references/<Repository>`. Stay attached until you finish, then stop the run
with `down`.

### Launch McpCli under a debugger

McpCli exits after each command, so launch the reported DLL under the debugger
instead of attaching. Offline discovery verbs (`modules`, `operations`,
`describe`) need no gateway URL. With [netcoredbg](https://github.com/Samsung/netcoredbg)
(MIT; verified with 3.2.0; download it outside the repository):

```bash
tool="<path reported by HXI010>"
netcoredbg --interpreter=cli -- dotnet "$tool" modules
# at the ncdb prompt:
#   break Hexalith.McpCli.Core.Catalog.CatalogService.ListModules
#   run
```

netcoredbg first reports the breakpoint as `--pending`, because the McpCli
assemblies are not loaded yet; it binds once `Hexalith.McpCli.Core` loads, and
`run` then stops in `ListModules`. A `file:line` breakpoint, such as the
absolute path of `CatalogService.cs` under `references/Hexalith.McpCli`, works
the same way.

In VS Code, use a `coreclr` launch configuration whose `program` is the
reported DLL and whose `args` are the McpCli arguments. Breakpoints bind to the
sources in `references/Hexalith.McpCli`. Until modules are enrolled, `modules`
returns `catalog_empty` with exit code `2`. The run-id directory in the
reported path is the `runId` for `down --run-id`.

### Own-repository AppHosts

A technical module's own AppHost, such as `src/Hexalith.Memories.AppHost` or
`src/Hexalith.EventStore.AppHost`, serves only that repository's own tests. A
run of it is never evidence that the module runs in the Platform composition;
only the commands above, from this workspace, are. McpCli has no AppHost: its
own `references/Hexalith.Platform` and any run from its repository root serve
only its own tests, and such a run is never Platform evidence.

## Verify Agents host contract (clean checkout)

From a clean clone of this repository:

```bash
./eng/verify-agents-host.sh
```

Expected: Release build of the platform AppHost succeeds, and the repository
declares itself as the Agents platform host without requiring any Agents-owned
hosting projects.

## Local run

```bash
aspire run
```

The Works migration topology is available when the sibling `works` checkout is
present. Enable it explicitly for local development:

```bash
Platform__Works__Enabled=true aspire run
```

The Works topology is a development preview while the AD-20 R1–R11 parity and
rollback gate remains open. The existing Works AppHost remains the supported
rollback composition until that gate passes.

# Enroll a domain module

The module owner uses this kit to prepare enrollment in Platform. Static validation
and the human demonstration are separate gates. The accepted published tool is
`4.35.2`, including ordinary declaration validation and the read-only `--adoption`
report. Copy the exact pin from the direct Platform checkout as described below.
[Release evidence](../_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/evidence/1-13/README.md)
records owner approval, gated publication and fresh acceptance. Static PASS rows
leave the owner's live SM-2 demonstration separately unverified.

## 1. Declare and initialize the minimum workspace

Use the module repository as the active Git root. Declare direct root submodules
in `.gitmodules`: `Hexalith.Platform`, `Hexalith.Builds`, `Hexalith.McpCli`,
`Hexalith.EventStore`, `Hexalith.Tenants`, `Hexalith.Memories`, and every additional
declared server dependency. Exclude the active module itself; the three minimum
server dependencies are distinct identities. Commit gitlinks at the selected
revisions. Use repository folders named `references/Hexalith.<id>`, compared
case-insensitively with the declared module identity. Add each missing direct
reference from the module root (replace the URL and ID):

```bash
git submodule add '<url>' 'references/Hexalith.<Id>'
```

Initialize the following minimum root paths at their recorded gitlinks, excluding
self; append every additional declared dependency's direct path to the command:

```bash
git -c submodule.recurse=false submodule update --init --checkout -- \
  references/Hexalith.Platform references/Hexalith.Builds references/Hexalith.McpCli \
  references/Hexalith.EventStore references/Hexalith.Tenants references/Hexalith.Memories
git submodule status
```

Never add `--recursive` or `--remote`. Do not initialize a direct dependency's own
`references/*`. An already initialized nested submodule fails validation; its owner
must deinitialize that exact path before proceeding. Keep each checkout HEAD equal
to its module root's recorded gitlink. A sibling checkout's presence has no effect.

## 2. Customize the declaration and inventory

Copy each starter file only when absent; merge an existing declaration or inventory
with owner review. Then replace the sample identities, app/resource/server
IDs, routes, topic names, configuration keys and readiness endpoint with the real
module contract. Keep all five groups: identity, runtime, surfaces, integration and
lifecycle. Dependencies name module identities, not repository paths. Add every
server dependency to both the declaration and the direct workspace references.
Readiness must describe the actual ready endpoint. The example declares a logical
pub/sub role, injected component key, explicit subscription route and dead-letter
topic; Platform assigns the physical scoped component names. Do not copy a literal
state-store, pub/sub or secret-store component name into code or configuration.

```bash
mkdir -p module
for file in hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json hosting-inventory.json platform-handoff.md sm-2-checklist.md; do
  if [ ! -e "module/$file" ]; then
    cp "references/Hexalith.Platform/templates/domain-module-enrollment/$file" "module/$file"
  fi
done
```

Inventory every existing module-owned `*.AppHost`, `*.Aspire` and
`*.ServiceDefaults` project by exact tracked `.csproj` path, kind, accountable owner
and consumers. Replace every pending owner and consumer with an identified value;
use `"consumers": ["none"]` only when no consumers exist. Unedited pending defaults
fail adoption validation; plans and gates may remain pending. Rename the sample
inventory entries to existing projects; remove entries for projects that do not
exist. Use `"projects": []` if there are none.
Do not create sample hosting projects. Keep existing projects frozen, with explicit
replacement and retirement plans and pending gates. Do not add cross-module wiring.

Inventory completeness grants no retirement authority. Retirement requires producer
adoption, owner-reviewed **source/package/deployed parity**, and, when applicable,
EventStore **AD-22 exact-subject consumer-removal authority**. Record exact evidence
and authorized subject; never infer permission from a successful static report.
Only exact frozen hosting-project directories are excluded from the Dapr audit.
A frozen directory's last segment must equal its project file name without the
extension (ignoring case), and it must contain no other project; use a dedicated
hosting-project directory.
Root build files and dependency checks always remain in scope.

## 3. Restore exactly the accepted tool

Merge only the `hexalith.builds.module.cli` tool entry from the **direct Platform
checkout**, preserving the exact version and disabled roll-forward as well as every
other local tool entry. Do not pick the newest NuGet version. For example, with
Python 3:

```bash
mkdir -p .config
python3 - <<'PYTHON'
import json
from pathlib import Path
accepted = json.loads(Path("references/Hexalith.Platform/.config/dotnet-tools.json").read_text())
path = Path(".config/dotnet-tools.json")
local = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {"version": 1, "isRoot": True, "tools": {}}
local.setdefault("tools", {})["hexalith.builds.module.cli"] = accepted["tools"]["hexalith.builds.module.cli"]
path.write_text(json.dumps(local, indent=2) + "\n")
PYTHON
dotnet tool restore
dotnet tool run hexalith-module --version
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- validate --manifest module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json
```

Run both adoption output modes with the restored accepted tool:

```bash
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- validate --manifest module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json --adoption
dotnet tool run hexalith-module -- validate --manifest module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json --adoption --output json
```

Every static requirement reports PASS/FAIL, file and reason. Failures produce a
nonzero exit while independent requirements are still checked. Validation is
read-only: it never initializes references, resolves a source mapping, restores
packages or starts resources. It inspects tracked module-owned source, build,
configuration and helper files. Add enrollment files to normal owner review so
that source scans see the intended tracked workspace.

## 4. Use the tool's source mapping and Dapr conventions

Remove sibling/ancestor/nested checkout discovery and package-fallback helpers.
Remove file-based dependency/mode selectors and module assignments to tool-owned
root/mode properties. Project/package pairs may consume `UseHexalithProjectReferences`
and the tool-provided `Hexalith*Root` values; only the tool selects source/Debug or
package/Release. Every `Hexalith*Root` and `Hexalith*FromSource` property name is
reserved for the tool, including names that describe the module's own repository.
Rename module-local properties, for example `HexalithProjectsRepositoryRoot` to
`ProjectsRepositoryDirectory`. An `Exists` guard on an unrelated optional import is legitimate.
An `Exists` guard that chooses a dependency, root or mode is forbidden. The sole
bootstrap exception is `HexalithBuildsRoot` defaulting to
`$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)references/Hexalith.Builds` only when that property is
empty; the tool supplies its mapping before this inert default is evaluated.

Read configured Dapr component names using declared configuration keys. Declare
subscriptions, delivery routes and dead-letter policy in the manifest. Remove
`[Topic]`, `WithTopic`, subscribe-handler mapping and `/dapr/subscribe` discovery.
Preserve module ACL files as authoritative inputs. Review local mTLS,
deny-by-default receiver ACLs and scoped components with the owner.

Leave the declared component key empty or use an injected placeholder; for example,
in `appsettings.json`:

```json
{ "Sample": { "Dapr": { "EventsComponent": "" } } }
```

Read the injected name from `IConfiguration`, for example
`configuration["Sample:Dapr:EventsComponent"]`, and pass that value to Dapr.
`${SAMPLE_EVENTS_COMPONENT}`, `$(Sample:Dapr:EventsComponent)` and
`{{ Sample.Dapr.EventsComponent }}` are also accepted placeholders for an external
configuration provider to replace. The static audit accepts these forms; Platform
injects the declared configuration key during the run.

The audit is a **bounded static check**, limited to known patterns in supported
tracked files up to 1 MiB each after file-type filtering. Every tracked `.cs`,
`.csproj`, `.props`, `.targets`, `.ps1`, `.sh` and `.py` file is in scope, including
tests and tracked evidence copies. The dependency audit inspects those extensions.
The Dapr audit inspects `.cs` files and configuration defaults in `appsettings*.json`,
`appsettings*.yaml` or `appsettings*.yml`. Only exact frozen hosting-project
directories are excluded from the Dapr audit. Other JSON/YAML files, including
evidence JSON and OpenAPI YAML, are not read.

An immediately asserted existence probe, such as `Directory.Exists(path).ShouldBeFalse()`
or `Assert.True(File.Exists(path))`, is verification and passes; the same probe in a
condition is rejected. Dapr API arguments and Dapr-specific names (`StateStoreName`,
`PubSubName`, `SecretStoreName`, `bindingName`) reject literal component names;
generic `StoreName`/`ComponentName` literals fail only in a Dapr context. `null` in
any case and `~` count as unset. The dependency audit also rejects sibling paths that
`Path.Combine`, `Path.Join`, `os.path.join` or `Join-Path` builds from `..` segments,
parent-directory imports that start outside the module, and reserved-property
overrides in scripts and `dotnet` arguments. Generic Dapr calls are matched up to one
nested level. Human source review must inspect unusual configuration filenames,
indirection, unsupported languages, generated code and any constructs outside that
bound. Passing rows cannot prove runtime behavior or replace SM-2.

## 5. Complete the accountable Platform registration handoff

Create `module/platform-handoff.md` from the copied template and identify the module
owner and Platform owner. Keep its status **pending** until the owners review the
implementation and attach evidence. A valid declaration, adoption PASS, or source
mapping does not register an executable. A new owner outside
`PlatformServerBindings.ReferenceProjects` will refuse with an unavailable mapped
project until Platform implements the binding.

The ordinary public runner has no caller `Projects` override. The internal
composition-run override used by tests is a test seam. Synthetic composition tests

# Hexalith Platform

## Why

**Vision to realize, driven by a pain.** Each Hexalith module wires its own hosting today: domain AppHosts, per-module Dapr plumbing, file-existence source switches. The only root composition is an opt-in Works preview, and no hosted Kubernetes or domain configuration exists. As a result, developers cannot reliably run the whole system, or one module with only its dependencies. CI has no shared real-service environment, and there is no gated, recoverable path to production. Hexalith Platform gives the internal team one solution for development, testing, staging and production. Platform owns shared hosting, composition, promotion and recovery; modules keep their domain behavior. It serves developers, team members using hosted environments (including through McpCli), automated CI workflows, Administrator (the production authority and recovery owner) and a named recovery deputy, who receives every notification and can restore, verify and reopen service when Administrator is unavailable. The designated Kubernetes installation and a shared Keycloak server already exist. The MVP proves the model on seven modules before the rest enroll through the same schema.

Mechanism authority is the adopted [architecture spine](../../planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-platform-2026-09-27/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md) (final, updated 2026-10-01). This spec cites its decisions as AD-1..AD-15 and its sections by name, and re-decides none of them.

## Capabilities

CAP-N maps one-to-one to PRD FR-N. Full testable consequences: [acceptance-criteria.md](acceptance-criteria.md).

- **CAP-1** — Complete local environment
  - **intent:** A developer starts the complete MVP environment locally through Platform to test and debug. It contains EventStore, Tenants, Parties, Folders, Projects, McpCli and Memories plus their supporting components.
  - **success:** All seven modules report module-owned readiness together within the effective startup deadline. The local McpCli client connects and executes enabled modules' agent-eligible operations through CLI and MCP, with no hosted McpCli service (SM-1). AD-1, AD-9, AD-13.
- **CAP-2** — Debug the active module checkout
  - **intent:** A developer runs and debugs a domain module from its own workspace, which includes Platform as a direct submodule, executing the checkout being edited. EventStore, Memories and McpCli are debugged from source in the Platform workspace.
  - **success:** Breakpoints and source changes affect the running code in each domain-module workspace (Tenants, Parties, Folders, Projects), and for EventStore, Memories and McpCli in the Platform workspace. Only the active root's direct `references/` declarations are initialized. Local runs use project references and Debug; CI uses NuGet and Release (SM-2). AD-4.
- **CAP-3** — Developer-defined minimum environment
  - **intent:** A module developer declares the servers the module needs for development and integration testing, and Platform composes exactly that minimum environment as real services.
  - **success:** The Parties workspace runs the active Parties checkout with EventStore, Tenants and Memories as its declaration specifies, and no unrelated domain module (SM-2). AD-1, AD-4.
- **CAP-4** — Real-service integration test environments
  - **intent:** A developer or CI workflow provisions the declared environment and runs integration tests against real services. Tests wait for readiness, data is isolated, and retention and cleanup are limited to what the run owns.
  - **success:** Local Aspire and CI runs pass module-defined checks. CI evidence identifies the candidate revision, expected artifact identities and the artifacts actually loaded. Controlled success, failure, startup-timeout, cancellation, collision, attachment, hold-expiry and withdrawal scenarios show the agreed ownership, retention and cleanup, with leftovers reported, diagnostics preserved and no other environment touched (SM-3). AD-4, AD-5, AD-10.
- **CAP-5** — Isolated tests without Platform
  - **intent:** A module developer runs isolated tests from the module's test project without starting Platform, using lightweight doubles where needed.
  - **success:** Isolated tests pass with no Platform or domain server running. CI runs them before integration tests, and an isolated pass never satisfies integration acceptance (SM-3). AD-5.
- **CAP-6** — Critical-flow staging gate
  - **intent:** Platform promotes a release to production, in either release mode, only after staging E2E tests pass for every enrolled module's critical flows, run against that exact release.
  - **success:** Every promoted release has complete passing staging evidence for that exact release and retained artifacts. Missing, skipped, failed, incomplete, stale or wrong-release results block promotion. Automatic promotion additionally needs G3, compatibility evidence against production's working baseline and a passing shared-infrastructure currency check (SM-5; SM-C1 = 0). AD-2, AD-7, AD-13, AD-15.
- **CAP-7** — Production deployment verification
  - **intent:** Platform verifies that a production deployment reaches readiness and passes module-owned production-safe smoke checks before declaring it working, and detects failure.
  - **success:** Rehearsals fire each failure trigger: rollout not ready within 10 minutes, 60 continuous seconds of unavailability, two consecutive smoke failures, and a missing result. Only a clean verification window yields a working release (SM-5). AD-2, AD-3, AD-7.
- **CAP-8** — Verified recovery to the previous working release
  - **intent:** Platform recovers an eligible failed compatible deployment once to the recorded working application without rewinding data, and controls approved empty, degraded or incompatible attempts through their recorded recovery paths.
  - **success:** A rehearsed automatic rollback restores readiness within 10 minutes and passes the five-minute verification using the restored release's smoke checks, with data intact. Rehearsals also prove retained-data compatibility or named data restore, per-cause promotion stops, admission reconciliation, first-install and failed or unverified paths, and no second automatic attempt. Administrator and the recovery deputy receive GitHub reports; only Administrator approves attempts and clears stops (SM-5; SM-C3 = 0). AD-2, AD-3, AD-15.
- **CAP-9** — Production backup and disaster recovery
  - **intent:** The recovery owner or the recovery deputy restores production onto prepared capacity from recovery points kept outside the primary failure domain, and verifies it before reopening.
  - **success:** An isolated drill proves RPO at most one hour and, for outages beginning within declared response coverage, RTO at most four hours from outage to verified service, including fencing, integrity, smoke, access, admission-revocation and erasure-safe tenant-key checks. Backup cadence, retention, monitoring and GitHub alerts to Administrator and the deputy are verified; post-cut grants are listed for Administrator rather than restored as authority (SM-6). AD-7, AD-12.
- **CAP-10** — Isolated staging and production
  - **intent:** Platform hosts the MVP modules in staging (`hexalith.com`) and production (`tache.ai`) on the designated installation, with separate application data and credentials.
  - **success:** Both environments expose the MVP interfaces. Negative tests from staging users, workloads, credentials, automation and pods reach no production data, secrets, ports, hostnames or administration (SM-4; SM-C2 = 0). AD-6, AD-8.
- **CAP-11** — Explicit production-user access
  - **intent:** Production access requires explicit admission, which only Administrator grants or revokes through an authenticated, auditable action. Staging authorization and recovery authority never confer it.
  - **success:** Staging-only users are denied production data and operations through the API, CLI and MCP. An authorized production user receives exactly their production permissions; admission revocation survives restoration, and reconciliation fails closed on record-chain or two-way membership mismatch (SM-4; SM-C2 = 0). AD-6, AD-14.
- **CAP-12** — Module operations through McpCli
  - **intent:** A user discovers and invokes enabled modules' agent-eligible commands and queries through the McpCli CLI or MCP, in a selected local, staging or production environment and under that environment's permissions.
  - **success:** Operations execute only in the selected environment, through its gateway. Ineligible (UI-only or confirmation-required), disabled-module, mismatched-contract and unauthorized operations are refused, and an empty executable catalog cannot satisfy acceptance (SM-1, SM-4). AD-11, AD-13, AD-14.

## Constraints

- **Cluster management.** Adopt the spine’s Cluster management convention: Rancher community on a dedicated private single-node K3s VM imports the existing kubeadm cluster. Manager/agents are shared infrastructure outside Aspire and the retained application chart; private administration, independent native access, qualified authority and management recovery are required. Preserve single-node/shared-host limitations. Retire KubeSphere before the supported hop, then qualify Rancher before staging (approved 2026-10-01 correction; AD-1/3/6/7/8/12).

- **Spine precedence.** The spine governs mechanism. Where it refines a PRD rule, the spine applies. AD changes go through bmad-architecture, never through this spec. The finalized PRD, addendum and architecture update 4 plus the approved 2026-10-01 Rancher correction are synchronized ([sequencing.md](sequencing.md#source-document-alignment)).
- **Ownership.** Platform owns shared hosting, composition, promotion and recovery. Modules own domain behavior, server lists, readiness semantics, public operations, critical flows, smoke suites and authoritative-state inventories. Platform implements no domain behavior and no second orchestration framework (AD-1).
- **Roles.** Only Administrator approves releases, clears promotion stops and grants or revokes production admission. The named recovery deputy receives every notification, holds independent recovery and key access, and may declare a stop, execute documented recovery, verify restoration and restore only the recorded pre-incident ingress state. The deputy cannot approve a release, clear a stop or administer admission; before G2, reopening keeps user ingress closed. Recovery never grants admission or roles (spine Roles, AD-6).
- **Single composition model.** One Platform-owned Aspire model, launched by the Platform tool, composes every environment. No AppHost runs in production. The retained application Helm package is the only staging and production deployment definition (AD-1, AD-2).
- **Platform tool and runner.** Builds' `hexalith-module` is the Platform tool (AD-4) and the runner (AD-10). Platform owns the declaration semantics and lifecycle rules; Builds implements them. Published versions through 4.27.4 and `hexalith.module-manifest.v1` are not Platform-accepted; the Platform declaration ships as the next manifest major (spine Module declaration).
- **Active-root dependencies.** Only the active root repository's direct `references/` declarations are initialized. No recursive or remote submodule updates; nested submodules stay uninitialized, and any initialized by accident are deinitialized. No ancestor, sibling or package fallback. Local builds use project references and Debug; CI/CD uses NuGet packages and Release (AD-4, AD-5).
- **Platform identity.** Every workspace other than Platform that runs the tool, McpCli included, declares `references/Hexalith.Platform`; its submodule commit is the Platform identity, and in the Platform repository the identity is HEAD. Package mode builds the composition from that submodule at a Platform release tag and refuses identity, Builds-catalog or tool-range mismatches; source mode warns. EventStore, Memories and McpCli produce Platform evidence only from the Platform workspace (AD-4).
- **Candidate CI identity.** Candidate evidence binds the declared committed revision and expected content identities to every candidate Release artifact the composition actually loads, including Contracts, server and extension packages, services, tools, packages inside the composed host and run-scoped McpCli. Missing identities, caches or substitutions from another build or revision, uncommitted inputs and labelled baseline-only runs cannot pass candidate acceptance. The shared Platform/Builds candidate-selection, gated-decision and evidence-reuse policy precedes acceptance (AD-4, AD-5).
- **Real services only.** Platform environments run only the configured real services. Test doubles exist only in module-owned isolated tests.
- **Readiness.** Each module defines readiness for its services. A running process is not readiness, and a required service without usable readiness evidence is a configuration error. The default test startup deadline is 10 minutes; only a justified finite override, shown in diagnostics, may change it.
- **Run-owned test environments (AD-10).**
  - Each suite or compatible batch gets a fresh run-owned environment, or fails naming the conflicting run. Explicit attach requires compatible composition, mode, artifact identities, readiness and isolation; hosted attachment fails, and post-owner-finish attachment is refused unless the local environment was retained after failure.
  - The owner outcome records immediately. Accepted attachments hold cleanup only until all end or their finite recorded hold expires. Hold expiry, owner cancellation or explicit stop withdraws affected attached runs; withdrawal is neither pass nor failure and is never integration evidence.
  - Local success cleans after attachment holds. A test or startup failure by the owner or any attached run retains the environment; later cancellation cannot erase that retention. Explicit developer cleanup remains available.
  - CI attachment stays within one job. Job completion or cancellation withdraws attached runs first, then always cleans all owned resources, including after partial provisioning.
  - Cleanup never touches another run or a hosted environment, reports leftovers, and results and diagnostics survive it.
- **Hosting.** The designated Kubernetes installation is `192.168.1.30`, with staging on `hexalith.com` and production on `tache.ai`. Supporting infrastructure may be shared only if application data, credentials and namespaces stay per environment (AD-8).
- **Identity.** The existing shared Keycloak hosts separate staging and production realms. Production admission is membership in the human production-admission group, granted only by Administrator: never by default, by promotion, or by copying staging membership. Synthetic actors use a separate synthetic-admission group limited to the synthetic tenant (AD-6, AD-14; spine Synthetic identities).
- **Same release digests.** Promotion ships the same retained package and image digests that passed staging. Evidence is bound to the exact release, and absent evidence is never a pass (AD-2).
- **Release modes.** *Automatic* needs G3, complete compatibility evidence and the shared-infrastructure currency check. *Administrator-approved* serves pre-G3 releases, SM-5 fault rehearsals before G2, empty or degraded production, and releases without demonstrated safe rollback. Empty means no working baseline; degraded means the last outcome was non-working or an incident, over-bound probe failure or failed health check shows production is not working. Reduced-recovery state is distinct. With retained application data, an approved attempt still needs valid evidence against its recorded baseline or a named data-restore recovery with acceptance checks, maximum duration and a usable post-lock recovery point. Only a first installation with no retained application data uses fresh-install proof. Common gates, lock, provenance, verification and records apply in both modes (RRA Release modes, Empty or degraded production; Production preconditions).
- **Production verification defaults.** Rollout must reach readiness within 10 minutes of deployment start, followed by a five-minute verification window. The deployment fails on 60 continuous seconds of unavailability, two consecutive smoke failures with the second 30 seconds after the first, or a missing result. One failed probe or one restart does not fail it. These defaults must be validated in staging; they are not availability guarantees.
- **Recovery paths.** An eligible compatible failure gets exactly one automatic application rollback: 10 minutes to readiness, then the same five-minute verification; it never cycles through older releases. A baseline re-deploy handles a failed automatic recovery. A named retained-data recovery uses the in-place data-restore form of the Recovery sequence. Replacement-capacity disaster recovery runs that sequence on the recovery executor. Each path becomes the working baseline only after its required verification (RRA Automatic recovery, In-place recovery, Recovery sequence; AD-7).
- **Recovery timing and fencing.** Resume and takeover preserve the attempt's original absolute and phase deadlines and remaining recovery allowance. A new epoch does not authorize mutation until every affected prior-epoch credential is revoked and its authority is fenced or drained; recovery-scope tasks commit only while their invoking epoch is current. Interrupted recovery re-enters through its own recovery-kind path (RRA Attempt ownership, Timing and interruption; Recovery sequence).
- **Promotion stop.** Stops are per environment and each new cause advances a monotonic revision. Production causes include every non-working outcome and recovery entry, failed pre-update health or over-bound probe failure, a recorded incident, a two-way admission/record mismatch, and an Administrator or deputy declaration. Monitoring sets and notifies but never clears. Administrator clearance uses compare-and-set against the observed revision, names every cause resolved or accepted, reviews lost-window handling and confirms admission matches; a later cause wins. An unaccepted continuing cause re-records after clear, while an accepted cause waits until it resolves and recurs (RRA Promotion stop).
- **Release tiers and records.** Every deployed object belongs to exactly one tier (application package, environment layer, shared infrastructure, outside every release) with one version authority. Application rollback touches only the application package. Records are accepted only when signed by their named writer, never by store access (AD-3; spine Release tiers; Binding classes and records).
- **NFR-1 rollback data safety.** Application rollback never rewinds business data, event history, credential rotations, revocations or key generations. Automatic releases must keep schemas and event formats compatible with the previous version. Incompatible releases use the Administrator-approved mode with a planned recovery (AD-3, AD-15).
- **NFR-2 recovery bounds.** RPO at most one hour, continuously. RTO at most four hours for outages beginning within declared response coverage, from outage to verified service, including detection, operator response and capacity. Coverage (time zone, primary and deputy responsibility, maximum acknowledgement time) is published before the first qualifying drill; deputy hours count only after the G2 deputy proof, and the outage clock never pauses. Backups run every 30 minutes, keeping frequent recovery points for seven days and daily points for 30 days, encrypted and outside the primary failure domain with independent access and decryption keys. Monitoring checks at least every 15 minutes and alerts when the newest usable point is over one hour old. Every point and restore covers each referenced non-erased tenant-key generation; current tombstone authority plus known lineage may prove an intentionally erased generation absent, which must never be restored. Unknown lineage or any unexplained missing generation fails closed. These are targets that have not yet been demonstrated (AD-12; RRA Recovery point and freshness, Detection and response).
- **NFR-3 isolation.** Isolation holds at service, data, routing and administration boundaries, including direct requests that bypass UIs and restored copies. It is verified by negative tests from staging users, workloads, credentials, automation identities and pods, plus a positive production-user test and denial after revocation (AD-8, AD-14).
- **Dapr boundary.** Dapr is the runtime infrastructure boundary. Only the named AD-9 exceptions (Memories FalkorDB graph, Memories Redis search/vector, the Memories SET NX preflight row) use provider SDKs. A new exception needs Administrator acceptance recorded in the spine (AD-9).
- **Executor isolation.** Staging, test or PR code never runs where production credentials are or were held. Deployments run on isolated per-environment executors from the private operations repository, whose only writers are the named writers; module-supplied code on an executor runs in a sandbox without job credentials (AD-7).
- **Notifications.** GitHub issues in a private notification repository, assigned to Administrator and mentioning the recovery deputy, are the single accepted notification path. Every deployment-failure, recovery, backup and monitor notification reaches both. Reporting keeps working while the primary environment is down (spine Diagnostics and notification).
- **MCP and CLI surfaces.** McpCli stdio is the only MVP MCP surface, and McpCli executes only agent-eligible operations. Legacy module and technical-module MCP hosts, plug-ins and CLIs, including EventStore Admin.Cli and .Admin.Mcp, are frozen: never enrolled, deployed, routed, mapped in an enrolled host or issued a realm client in any Platform composition, and retired only with the AD-11 evidence. Any new MCP/CLI surface or transport, including McpCli HTTP, needs a Platform AD under AD-14 (AD-11, AD-14).
- **G1.** Production is first deployed with ingress closed, admitting only executor and probe sources, with an empty human production-admission group, on a supported Kubernetes minor, with GitHub delivery working. Before G2, Administrator may temporarily grant one designated synthetic identity, limited to the synthetic tenant, solely for SM-4 positive evidence; its record expires no later than G2 and its revocation is followed by a denial check. This does not open G2 ([sequencing.md](sequencing.md)).
- **G2.** Production users are admitted and ingress opens only after the AD-12 drill passes, including Memories tombstone and key continuity; SM-4 isolation and access checks pass; and recovery access, capacity, deputy alert delivery and response coverage are verified. Admitting the first user is an access-configuration change: SM-4 is re-verified on the live realm with that user before anyone else is admitted. The PRD's "before production use" means G2: SM-4 and SM-6 are its entry evidence.
- **G3.** Automatic promotion is enabled only after the SM-5 rehearsals pass; this is the PRD's "before enabling automatic production promotion". A change to verification, recovery or rollback-set policy suspends it until the affected rehearsals repeat. Before G3, every production release uses the Administrator-approved mode.
- **First shared versions and Owned work gates.** Module adoption epics wait for the First shared versions artifacts they consume, and remaining work lands at its spine Owned work gate. Shared candidate/attachment policy precedes CI evidence; monitor and admission bounds precede G1; reduced-recovery operating policy precedes G2; shared-infrastructure currency policy precedes G3. Each artifact or policy exists and is qualified before the consumer or gate it controls ([sequencing.md](sequencing.md)).
- **Source precedence.** The Platform MVP recovery envelope governs the stricter infrastructure clauses of Folders and Projects without blocking their enrollment. Module behavior, authorization, data-safety and release gates are never waived.
- **Evidence.** Deferring work assigns it; it never turns absent evidence into a pass. These are target requirements. A document marked final does not establish an implemented capability, a passed runtime check or a production qualification.

## Non-goals

- A generic Platform mocking subsystem, fake-service catalogue, or per-service real/fake switches. If a concrete test later needs a substitute service, that case is assessed on its own.
- Standalone module workspaces for EventStore, Memories or McpCli; their source debugging stays in the Platform workspace.
- Rollback triggered by traffic metrics (error rate, latency) in the MVP.
- Automatically reversing business data or event history on rollback, switching releases indefinitely, or automatically handling failures found after the verification window; those are operational incidents.
- An emergency release path that skips the staging gate, including after DR.
- A standby production installation, automatic infrastructure failover, HA or warm standby, multiple regions, broker changes, scaling work or in-transit TLS for every data service without a measured requirement.
- A numeric uptime percentage, latency or throughput targets, 24/7 response, or a cost target.
- MCP and CLI surfaces beyond McpCli stdio and its CLI head: hosted HTTP MCP, McpCli HTTP, Memories.Mcp, Parties.Mcp, FrontComposer MCP, EventStore Admin tools; step-up or confirmation flows through McpCli; system-initiated cross-module operations without a user actor. Each needs an AD first.
- Platform maintaining a central list of critical flows or smoke suites, or its own business implementations of module operations.
- Including servers outside the MVP set (e.g. Agents, ChatBot, Conversations, Timesheets, Works) in MVP acceptance. They stay in longer-term scope and will enroll through the same declaration schema.
- The Projects G-1 durable task engine; the HA, RPO-0 or 15-minute RTO infrastructure guarantees in Folders and Projects documents; a custom orchestration DSL, environment service or per-dependency retry policy.

## Success signal

- A developer debugs Parties from its own workspace against real EventStore, Tenants and Memories. A release that passed staging E2E for that exact release reaches `tache.ai` through G1, G2 and G3. A rehearsed failure rolls back once with data intact, and a drill restores production within a one-hour RPO and, for an outage within declared response coverage, a four-hour RTO.
- Each SM-1..SM-6 demonstration is recorded with release, environment, result and diagnostics, and SM-C1..SM-C4 stay at zero ([success-measures.md](success-measures.md)).

# Architecture Spine — Hexalith Platform

## Design Paradigm

**Modular composition root over event-driven domain services.** Platform composes environments and their operational policies. Technical modules own reusable runtime capabilities; domain modules own contracts, behavior, projections, authorization policy and service-specific readiness. Event-sourced aggregate mutation uses the EventStore SDK. Platform implements no domain behavior and no second orchestration framework.

The MVP covers EventStore, Tenants, Parties, Folders, Projects, McpCli and Memories plus their declared supporting capabilities. **Technical modules:** EventStore, Memories, Commons, Builds, FrontComposer, PolymorphicSerializations. **Domain modules:** Tenants, Parties, Folders, Projects and later domain modules. **Tool:** McpCli. A domain module's minimum composition is EventStore, Tenants, Memories and the servers its declaration's enabled server list specifies; source or package mode follows AD-4. Domain modules keep domain UIs, thin SDK hosts and EventStore extension packages; they own no AppHost, Aspire or ServiceDefaults infrastructure, and existing ones follow Migration and coexistence. Technical modules may own reusable hosting capabilities.

**Roles.** **Administrator** is the production authority, recovery owner and Platform architecture owner; only Administrator approves releases, clears the promotion stop and administers production admission. The named **recovery deputy** receives every deployment-failure, recovery, backup and monitor notification, holds independent recovery and key access, and may execute documented recovery, verify restoration and reopen service, whether or not Administrator is available. While Administrator is unavailable, nobody can revoke production admission; the deputy's containment tools are the promotion stop and documented recovery. Reopening follows Recovery sequence step 7. **Named writers** of the operations repository are Administrator and the second Hexalith organization owner.

**Terms.** An unprefixed AD-n is this spine's; other modules' decisions carry their module name (EventStore AD-11). PRD glossary terms apply, including G1–G3 (Production entry gates), SM-n success measures and response coverage. The **Platform tool** and **runner** are Builds' `hexalith-module`. **Mode** is source (local, Debug) or package (CI, Release). The **application package**, **environment layer** and **shared infrastructure** are defined in Release tiers; **attempt**, **lock** and **epoch** in Attempt ownership; attempt kinds in Timing and interruption; **recovery mode** in Recovery sequence; the **rollback set** and **rollback generation** in AD-15. Binding classes, record kinds and the **working baseline** are defined in Binding classes and records; the lifecycle states evidence-validated, release-available and production-promoted are EventStore AD-11's. The **gateway** is the composed `eventstore` host's authenticated endpoint; a **Gateway** is an environment's Gateway API object. **CI** means module and Platform test workflows, never the publication workflow. The Builds package "release record" is distinct from this spine's release record.
